Subject: Request: promotional credit + packaging change for pilot

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. We loved the latency profile and the KV caching behavior — good fit for our inference pipeline. Before the execs greenlight a pilot, procurement asked me to get clarity on two items: a) whether Redwood can provide a staged discount (pilot -> ramp) with a small promotional credit to offset onboarding engineering hours, and b) whether we can remove the dedicated VPC add-on from the initial pilot pricing and add it later if we scale.

The rough numbers they shared: 3-month pilot (~$60k list run-rate) with an expected 6–9 month ramp to $250k ARR if metrics hold. They're asking for a 20% pilot discount + a one-time $8k onboarding credit. They also want the VPC add-on excluded for the pilot and treated as an optional add-on post-pilot.

Can you confirm if Redwood has precedent for this structure and next steps to get a formal exception on discounting? I'm attaching our short procurement note.

Appreciate it,
Sarah Liang
Head of Procurement — NovaMed AI

Hi Sarah — great to hear and thanks for the clear ask. We have a couple of internal approval levers for pilot promotions like this, but anything with a material onboarding credit and an outside default on packaging typically requires VP/CFO review for a one-off exception.

I will: 
- Run the preliminary economics with Finance and Sales Ops (attached: pricing-model-novamed.xlsx)
- Draft an exception memo for exec signoff (cc Marissa from Revenue Ops)
- Confirm acceptable language for removing the VPC add-on for the pilot period

Can you confirm the desired pilot start date window (early Dec vs mid-Dec) and whether NovaMed needs the credit to be applied upfront as invoice credit or as a rebate at the end of pilot? That will change the accounting treatment.

Best,

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding NovaMed's procurement ask. Key asks: 20% pilot discount on ~60k run-rate, $8k one-time onboarding credit, and temporarily remove VPC add-on from pilot SKU.

I've attached the initial pricing model I ran to show unit economics at pilot vs ramp. High level: with 20% pilot discount + $8k credit our blended unit margin drops ~9pp for the 3-month window but recovers quickly at expected ramp. Recommendation idea: offer a staged discount schedule (20% pilot, 12% first 6 months after pilot, revert to standard at scale) and make the onboarding credit contingent on a signed 6-month renewal.

Requesting: 
- Marissa, can Revenue Ops draft a short exception memo that we can present to VP/CFO with economic sensitivity and proposed guardrails (commitments, clawback if no conversion)?
- Karthik, can you flag any compliance/contracting pitfalls with removing VPC from pilot SKU (SLA/ops implications)?

Attachments: pricing-model-novamed.xlsx

Thanks — I can present the memo to leadership if you want me to own the write-up.

Jonas

Team — I put together a short exception memo and an economic sensitivity table. Attached: SOW_redwood_draft.pdf (SOW language proposing VPC as an optional add-on post-pilot), exception-memo-novamed.docx (attached in Drive link), and the same pricing-model-novamed.xlsx with scenario tabs. Highlights and proposed guardrails: 

- Proposed structure: 20% off list for the 3-month pilot; $8k onboarding credit (applied as invoice credit at pilot start); staged discount schedule post-pilot: 12% for months 1–6 after pilot, then standard pricing thereafter.
- Commitment: 6-month minimum term following pilot (to trigger staged discount); full conversion clause within 30 days of pilot end.
- Clawback: if NovaMed terminates without 6-month conversion, onboarding credit recouped pro rata on final invoice.
- VPC: treat as optional add-on; for pilot use shared-hosted environment with an approved SOC 2 config; include dedicated VPC language in SOW for later activation and billing change.
- Economics: with conservative conversion (40% of projected ramp), net LTV payback is neutral within 9 months; worst-case (20% conversion) pushes payback to ~15 months.

Action requested: VP/CFO signoff on exception (discount + credit) and approval for the SOW language. I've flagged the memo for finance review (cc'd). If Finance can pre-approve the invoice-credit accounting treatment, we can avoid a month-end revenue recognition issue.

I can convert the memo to the formal signoff template for VP/CFO e-sign if needed.

Marissa Cole

Thanks, Marissa — this memo looks thorough. Two quick notes from Contracting/Compliance: 

1) Removing VPC for pilot is acceptable provided we include explicit security controls and an approved SOC 2 baseline in the SOW. Ops will need 5 business days to provision any exceptions for shared-hosted onboarding.
2) On the $8k onboarding credit: Finance prefers invoice credit applied at pilot start (reduces receivable complexity). We should include the clawback language Marissa proposed and a clear renewal-trigger clause in the master services agreement (MSA).

I'm looping in VP Finance (vp-finance@redwood.ai) and CFO (cfo@redwood.ai) for approval. Recommended approval ask for execs: 
- Approve staged discount schedule and $8k onboarding invoice credit (one-off exception)
- Approve SOW language to treat VPC as optional add-on for pilot and signoff on required SOC 2 baseline

Jonas / Marissa — please attach the exception memo PDF + scenario tab and I'll follow with a short approval request email to VP/CFO (copying legal).

Karthik Iyer
Head of Contracts & Compliance | karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
